newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway Central Bank says curbing intervention.
newsitem.headline: Norway Central Bank says curbing intervention.

text.p: Norway's Central Bank said on Friday it would not intervene on the foreign exchange market for some time to try and dampen a strongly appreciating crown.
In a statement announcing a second interest rate cut in two days, the bank said it would now significantly reduce its interventions in the foreign exchange market.
"...in the light of developments in the foreign exchange market, Norges Bank will not intervene to any substantial extent in the foreign exchange market over a period," the bank said.
The bank said it had reduced its overnight deposit and overnight lending rate by 25 basis points to 3.25 percent and 5.25 percent respectively.
On Thursday the bank cut rates by 50 basis points.

"Since the reduction in interest rates on January 8, the crown has continued to appreciate against European currencies and Norges Bank has had to intervene heavily in the market with a view to stabilising the exchange rate," the statement said.
The bank said it had bought foreign currency equivalent to 20 billion crowns since the start of 1997.
